precepts.text: Joseph foretold the seven years of plenty and seven of famine.
precepts.point: Joseph saved Israel in the famine and Joshua of Ephraim divided the land. Ephraim therefore felt more entitled than Judah, and the rivalry began long before the split.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
The division between Ephraim and Judah did not begin at the split of the kingdom; it was building long before. Part of it goes back to Joseph, the father of Ephraim.

Joseph was raised up to tell Pharaoh what was coming: “Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land”, and “it shall be very grievous”. “And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.” Joseph prophesied the famine and showed Egypt how to prepare for it, and by it Israel was saved when Jacob and his sons ran down to Egypt.

The same pattern ran through Abraham. After the Lord told him, “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house”, he came from Ur of the Chaldees beyond the Euphrates, up to Haran, and down into Canaan, the stretch called the Fertile Crescent. When famine struck Canaan, Abraham ran to Egypt too, just as Jacob and his house later did. The parallels line up.

So Joseph’s house carried a great deal: Joseph saved Israel in the famine, and later Joshua, of Ephraim, divided the land. That is part of why Ephraim felt more entitled than Judah, and why the rivalry that tore the kingdom in two was already there long before Rehoboam.

precepts.text: Esau took Ishmael's daughter to spite his father, and Jacob's seed was promised to spread to the four corners.
precepts.point: Joseph saved Israel in the famine and Joshua of Ephraim divided the land. Ephraim therefore felt more entitled than Judah, and the rivalry began long before the split.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother”, Esau, seeing “that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father”, went his own rebellious way anyway. “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”. That is how Ishmael and Esau started intermingling, and that is where the light-skinned Arabs come from.

Jacob went toward Haran, and at a certain place he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, “and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” The Lord promised, “the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. That is all four corners: before they were even born, it was prophesied that Jacob’s seed would be found in the four corners of the earth, scattered among the families of the earth, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.” And the Lord promised, “I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.”

Jacob said, “this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven”, a portal to paradise. He set up his stone for a pillar, poured oil on it, “And he called the name of that place Beth–el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.” He vowed the tenth, the tithe.

Keep Bethel in mind. On the map it sits right under Shechem, the place where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan and where Rehoboam was later crowned. These early holy places all lay in the land that would become Ephraim’s.

precepts.text: Joshua was valiant in the wars and set Israel in their inheritance.
precepts.point: Joseph saved Israel in the famine and Joshua of Ephraim divided the land. Ephraim therefore felt more entitled than Judah, and the rivalry began long before the split.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua. He fought for us to gain the land and possession promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones who did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, as David did later as king.

Joshua 8 shows him valiant in the wars. At Ai, when the men of the city looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising to heaven, “they had no power to flee this way or that way”, and Israel smote them until none remained: twelve thousand fell that day. “And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide”, and they raised a great heap of stones over him at the gate.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron”. All Israel, “as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”, stood “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, and there they received the blessings and the cursings of the law.

Ebal and Gerizim, like Ai, Bethel and Shechem, are in Ephraim’s land. And Joshua himself was of Ephraim. The one who set Israel in their inheritance and divided the land came from that tribe, which is part of why Ephraim felt so entitled.

precepts.text: The tabernacle was set up at Shiloh, in Ephraim.
precepts.point: Joseph saved Israel in the famine and Joshua of Ephraim divided the land. Ephraim therefore felt more entitled than Judah, and the rivalry began long before the split.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” From there each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Shechem at the top, and Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, where the law’s blessings and curses were received. Bethlehem and Jerusalem lie further down, in Judah. All of Israel’s earliest places of worship were in Ephraim’s land: Abraham’s first altar at Shechem, Bethel, the mountains of the law, and the tabernacle at Shiloh.

So Ephraim felt entitled. They had the places of worship, the historical landmarks, and they were more in number than Judah. That is where the beef started, the buildup of the dividing hatred.

It broke open with Rehoboam. “And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king”, crowned at the very place of Abraham’s first altar. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke of taxes on the people to build sanctuaries of heathen worship for his wives. The old men who had served with Solomon said, lift it and they will serve you forever; Rehoboam “forsook the old men’s counsel” and listened to the young men he grew up with: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” It was so “for the cause was from the Lord”, to fulfill what Ahijah the Shilonite told Jeroboam when he tore the garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten.

Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Rehoboam’s tax collector, and made Jeroboam king. Only Judah, with Benjamin at its side, followed the house of David. When Rehoboam gathered an army, the Lord said, do not fight your brethren, “for this thing is from me.” The split was the Lord’s doing, and its roots ran back to the land at Shiloh.

precepts.text: The Most High called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him.
precepts.point: Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.
precepts.why:
The Most High told Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred and from his father's house. Isaiah says how he was called: “Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.”

He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go.

precepts.text: Confess Christ before men though it set you at variance with your own household; he that loveth father or mother more than Him is not worthy of Him.
precepts.point: Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.
precepts.why:
Getting out from your kindred and your father's house is what Christ asks too. “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Confessing Christ before men means something.

“Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.” He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.” As Abram left his kindred when he was called, do not let family or friends hold you back from the call.

precepts.text: Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; that confession means something.
precepts.point: Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.
precepts.why:
The confession Christ wants before men is Peter's. When Christ asked, “Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?” they answered, “Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.” Then he asked, “But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

That confession means something. Whoever confesses him before men, he confesses before his Father. Abram was called out alone from his country and kindred; confessing Christ before men, even against your own household, is the same going out.

precepts.text: Ye are the children of the prophets and of the covenant made with Abraham; unto you first God sent His Son to bless you in turning you from your iniquities.
precepts.point: In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
precepts.why:
“in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed” is not talking about everybody. Peter says who the promise is to: “Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed. Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.”

The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth. Through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not: God sent his Son to bless them in turning every one of them from his iniquities.

precepts.text: The Most High raised up prophets from the sons of Israel; the children of the prophets are the children of Israel.
precepts.point: In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
precepts.why:
Who are the children of the prophets? “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.”

The Most High raised up prophets from the sons of Israel, so the children of the prophets are the children of Israel. The families of the earth blessed in Abraham are Israel scattered into all nations, getting the chance to repent and return.

precepts.text: Pharaoh gave Abram livestock and menservants and maidservants; this is where the household's wealth and Hagar came from.
precepts.point: Their substance was so great they could not dwell together. That substance came from Egypt, where Pharaoh entreated Abram well for Sarai's sake and gave him sheep, oxen, servants, and camels; the maidservants from Egypt are where Hagar comes from.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
Where did all that substance come from? Egypt. When Sarai was taken into Pharaoh’s house, Pharaoh “entreated Abram well for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he asses, and menservants, and maidservants, and she asses, and camels.”

That is the wealth of the household in Genesis 13: “their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together.” The flocks and herds that the herdmen of Abram and the herdmen of Lot strove over were the livestock Pharaoh gave for Sarai’s sake.

The maidservants from Egypt matter too. That is where Hagar comes from: an Egyptian maidservant brought into the household when Pharaoh gave Abram menservants and maidservants.

precepts.text: Unto thy seed will I give this land; the promise was made at Abram's first altar.
precepts.point: This is the same covenant language spoken over the children of Israel: as the sand of the sea which cannot be measured nor numbered.

note.label: Genesis 13: The Peacemaker and the Promise

precepts.why:
This is the Most High reiterating the promise He made when Abram first entered the land. Back then “the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land”, and Abram built his first altar there to the Lord who appeared to him.

Now, after Lot was separated from him, the Lord tells him to look northward, southward, eastward and westward: “all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.” Same promise, same land, spoken again with the whole length and breadth of it laid out before him.

precepts.text: The saying began at Egypt: they will kill me, but save thee alive; say thou art my sister.
precepts.point: Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety.
precepts.why:
“She is my sister” was not new in Gerar. It began entering Egypt. Abram said to Sarai, “Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon: Therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive. Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.”

The fear was the same in Gerar: that the men of the place would kill him for his wife’s sake. And Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety, which is why Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took her.

precepts.text: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai; it happened both times she was taken.
precepts.point: The same happened with Pharaoh before. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet's wife; He does not play about that.
precepts.why:
Behind the scenes “the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abraham’s wife.” The same thing happened the first time she was taken: “the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.”

Both times, the whole house suffered. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet’s wife; He does not play about that. And when Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants, and they bare children.

precepts.text: The Most High told Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred; he separated Abram from the idolaters.
precepts.point: Jacob answered that he went away because he was afraid Laban would take his daughters from him by force, and said, With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

precepts.why:
“Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee”.

Here is why the Most High separated Abram from his country and his kindred: they served other gods. Laban, of the house of Nahor, asking Jacob “wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?” shows what that kindred was, idolaters. The Most High separated Abram because of what He had set up for Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and for us, that we not be idolaters.

precepts.text: There was a famine in the land, and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was grievous.
precepts.point: This is a repeating thing in our history: when famine came, the fathers moved toward Egypt for sustenance and nourishment. There was a famine in Abram's days and he went down into Egypt, and another famine in Isaac's days, when the Lord told him not to go down.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

precepts.why:
“And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there; for the famine was grievous in the land.” This is a repeating thing in our history: when famine came, the fathers moved toward Egypt for sustenance and nourishment. There was a famine in Abram’s days and he went down into Egypt.

Now in Jacob’s days it is the same. Jacob heard there was corn in Egypt and sent his sons down thither to buy, “that we may live, and not die.” Egypt was where the bread was in the famine, for Abram and for Jacob.

precepts.text: The same word came to Abraham: get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred; there were things the Lord had to do for him that required letting go.
precepts.point: What can we learn from this? You have to be willing to let go of some people. The Lord said, of whom I say, this shall not go with thee, the same shall not go: some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go.

note.label: Judges 7: The Three Hundred: The Victory Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
What can we learn from the trying at the water? You have to be willing to let go of some people. The Lord said, “of whomsoever I say unto thee, This shall not go with thee, the same shall not go.”

The same word came to Abraham: “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee.” There were things the Lord had to do for him that required letting go of his kindred and his father's house. Some people are not going to be beneficial to the war ahead of you, and the Lord will move them out of the way, but you have to be ready to let them go.

precepts.text: The Most High makes of Abraham a great nation, and in him all families of the earth are blessed.
precepts.point: The covenant was made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, and confirmed to Jacob as an everlasting covenant, giving Israel the land of Canaan as their inheritance.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
This is the covenant “which he made with Abraham”: “I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.”

The Most High makes of Abraham a great nation, and in him all families of the earth are blessed. That covenant was sworn to Isaac and confirmed to Jacob “for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant”, with the land of Canaan as Israel's inheritance.

And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee. That is why I read that with Rahab. Because people try to say that God just wants to kill everybody. No. If you are on our side, you could come along for the ride. He said, I will bless them that bless you and curse them that curse you. And some of you all think that you all are going to curse us and get away with it with no consequences.

A famine sent Abram into Egypt, as it would send Jacob later, and the Lord plagued Pharaoh's house over Sarai; here Abraham acquired Hagar, and here, by Josephus, he taught the Egyptians arithmetic and astronomy and confuted their divided customs.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: God told Abraham to get out of his country, from his kindred and his father's house, unto a land that I will show thee. Abraham was in Ur of the Chaldees, ancient Babylon; God told him to leave and go to a land he would give to him and his descendants.
I will make of thee a great nation, and make thy name great. I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee.

In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed: when we break that down, the all families is Israel scattered throughout the four corners of the earth. In the beginning the Most High is prophesying Israel being scattered through the four corners of the earth, because the Lord knew what would happen to us.

Abram built altars at Sichem and between Bethel and Hai, in what became the hill country of Ephraim, northern kingdom land. The dividing hatred between Ephraim and Judah is why both fell, the northern kingdom first and the southern after.
